verdict.rationale: OpenTofu's plan-then-apply workflow fits the story. Infrastructure is defined as text configuration an agent can write, `tofu plan` previews proposed changes, and speculative plans let you check changes before review. `-out=FILE` saves a plan that is only executed when you later pass it to `tofu apply`, which gives a natural approval gate. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of headless/non-interactive flags or machine-readable plan output, any agent-oriented docs (llms.txt and docs markdown return 404), and independent hands-on corroboration of an agent-driven plan/approve loop.
